It also reported that Bing no longer reproduced Disney's wording or logo [e2]. This November account does not establish whether an intended name restriction failed in Bing during December 1–29, 2023, leaving the claim unresolved [e2].
limitations: No verified December record establishes both the relevant Bing safeguard's intended coverage and a failure within that coverage.
The reported November improvement does not establish full reliability or December behavior.
The packet lacks deployment records and comprehensive testing that could rule out the claimed failures.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: DALL-E's proper-name blocking safeguards against infringement are not fully reliable.

statement.excerpt: Dall-E already has one minor safeguard in place – proper names (and hence deliberate infringement attempts) reportedly sometimes get blocked – but those safeguards aren’t fully reliable:
statement.document_title: Things are about to get a lot worse for Generative AI

our_interpretation: In context, this concerns DALL-E accessed through Bing, rather than assuming that Bing and ChatGPT had identical safeguards.
I use December 1–29, 2023 as the latest contemporaneously observable month before publication. The post supplies no exact experiment dates.
The ordinary reading is that a proper-name safeguard existed but could fail to prevent the targeted character or work from being generated.
Acceptance of a name outside the safeguard's intended coverage would not, by itself, establish a failure.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary records establish the relevant name-blocking safeguard and document at least one failure or bypass involving a name or work it was intended to restrict.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Authoritative deployment records and sufficiently comprehensive testing establish that the claimed failures did not occur, or that the purported safeguard did not exist in the specified deployment.
